title: High genomic diversity of dengue virus strains in Latin America and Asia-Pacific: insights from a phase 2 mosnodenvir clinical trial

analysis.research_question_and_background: Genomic surveillance of dengue virus (DENV) strains remains limited and regionally confined, despite advances in disease monitoring. This study aimed to assess the genomic diversity of circulating DENVs in Latin America and Asia-Pacific regions.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A Phase 2 clinical trial (NCT05201794) of mosnodenvir prophylaxis was conducted in endemic regions of Asia-Pacific and Latin America between 2023 and 2024. The study involved 411 dengue index cases (ICs) across 30 sites in 7 countries.
analysis.methods: DENV serotypes were determined using RT-PCR, and whole-genome sequencing was conducted for a subset of ICs (n = 150) representing DENV serotypes observed over time at 30 sites across 7 countries.
analysis.main_results: Cocirculation of all four DENV serotypes was observed in both Latin America and Asia-Pacific regions. DENV-1 was the predominant serotype (51.1%), with significant geographical variations in genotype distribution. Increased circulation of DENV-3 and DENV-4 strains was identified in Latin America during 2023–2024.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study captured a broad cross-section of contemporary DENV diversity circulating across Latin America and the Asia-Pacific region during 2023–2024, highlighting the dynamic nature of DENV evolution and spread.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings underscore the need for genomic surveillance to inform public health preparedness and mitigate dengue risk, particularly in regions with frequent virus (re)-introductions that may trigger new epidemics.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on a clinical trial population, which may not fully represent the broader DENV circulation in the general population. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the observational nature of the data.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed the genomic diversity of dengue virus (DENV) strains in Latin America and Asia-Pacific regions using data from a Phase 2 clinical trial of mosnodenvir prophylaxis. The trial involved 411 dengue index cases (ICs) across 30 sites in 7 countries, with whole-genome sequencing performed on 150 ICs. Results showed cocirculation of all four DENV serotypes in both regions, with DENV-1 being the most prevalent (51.1%). Increased circulation of DENV-3 and DENV-4 was observed in Latin America during 2023–2024. The study highlights the importance of genomic surveillance for public health preparedness, as it captured a broad cross-section of contemporary DENV diversity. However, the findings are based on a clinical trial population, which may not fully represent general DENV circulation, limiting the strength of the evidence to moderate.

title: Dengue among febrile patients in Ghana: prevalence and facility-level variation in a multisite surveillance study

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue is under-recognized in Ghana, where laboratory testing is limited. We estimated dengue NS1 and/or IgM positivity among febrile patients and described geographical, temporal, and demographic variation.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We conducted cross-sectional surveillance among consenting febrile patients aged [≥]1 year at six public facilities in Greater Accra, Bono East, and Upper West between August 2023 and July 2025. We randomly selected one region within each of three ecological strata and selected facilities with high febrile-case volumes. We approached and recruited consecutive eligible patients.
analysis.methods: We tested serum for dengue NS1 antigen and IgM antibody by ELISA; positive NS1 samples underwent RT-PCR and serotyping. We estimated proportions with 95% confidence intervals (CI) and used logistic regression to examine adjusted associations.
analysis.main_results: Among 2,936 participants, 204 were NS1- and/or IgM-positive (6.95%; 95% CI, 6.05-7.93%): 31 were NS1-only, 161 IgM-only, and 12 dual-positive. Prevalence ranged from 3.88% (95% CI, 2.19-6.31%) at Kintampo to 12.32% (9.56-15.55%) at Atebubu, both in Bono East. Adjusted odds increased with age (aOR per five years, 1.09; 95% CI, 1.05-1.14). Eight of 43 NS1-positive samples contained dengue RNA: five DENV-1 from Bono East and three DENV-3 from Upper West. There was no clear rainy-dry season difference.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Dengue NS1 and/or IgM were detected among febrile patients at all six facilities, and RT-PCR confirmed circulation of DENV-1 and DENV-3.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support including dengue in febrile illness evaluation and strengthening laboratory-supported surveillance in Ghana.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific limitations to the study design or evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to estimate dengue NS1 and/or IgM positivity among febrile patients in Ghana and describe geographical, temporal, and demographic variation. A cross-sectional surveillance was conducted at six public facilities in Greater Accra, Bono East, and Upper West between August 2023 and July 2025, involving 2,936 participants. Serum samples were tested for dengue NS1 antigen and IgM antibody using ELISA, with positive NS1 samples further analyzed by RT-PCR and serotyping. The results showed that 204 participants (6.95%) were NS1- and/or IgM-positive, with prevalence varying across sites. RT-PCR confirmed the circulation of DENV-1 and DENV-3. The findings highlight the need to include dengue in febrile illness evaluation and enhance laboratory-supported surveillance in Ghana. The study's limitations are not explicitly reported in the supplied evidence.

title: Epidemiología del dengue en Santo Domingo 2021-2025

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to analyze the temporal behavior of dengue notifications in the province of Santo Domingo de los Tsáchilas from 2021 to 2025 to identify weekly and annual variations.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective, descriptive, and observational ecological time series study was conducted based on aggregated epidemiological records.
analysis.methods: Data were organized by year and epidemiological week in Microsoft Excel and processed using IBM SPSS Statistics, version 27, with descriptive statistics.
analysis.main_results: A total of 15,744 dengue notifications were analyzed. The highest weekly concentration was observed in 2023, mainly between epidemiological weeks 28 and 46; in 2024, the highest frequencies were recorded during the first half of the year. The annual distribution showed that 2023 had 6,312 notifications (40.09%) and 2024, 5,890 (37.41%), which together represented 77.50% of the total. In 2025, 1,385 notifications were recorded, a 76.49% reduction from 2024.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings provided a descriptive reference for provincial epidemiological monitoring and the planning of surveillance and prevention actions. It was recommended to incorporate climatic, entomological, virological, and socio-environmental variables in future research.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study's findings can inform the surveillance and planning of actions for dengue prevention and control in the province.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the retrospective nature and the reliance on aggregated data, which may limit the generalizability of the findings. The evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed dengue notifications in Santo Domingo de los Tsáchilas from 2021 to 2025, identifying weekly and annual variations. The highest concentrations were observed in 2023 and 2024, with a significant reduction in 2025. The findings provide a reference for surveillance and prevention.

title: Foundation models capture human and environmental context to improve dengue forecasting

analysis.research_question_and_background: Accurate and timely probabilistic dengue forecasts can support public health preparedness, but producing reliable forecasts across locations and time horizons remains challenging.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We evaluated five statistical, machine-learning, deep-learning, and foundation-model approaches for forecasting monthly reported dengue cases across 5,570 Brazilian municipalities at 1-, 3-, 6- and 12-month horizons, with forecasts backtested from January 2020 to August 2025.
analysis.methods: We then tested whether spatial representations of human and environmental context from a Population Dynamics Foundation Model (PDFM) could improve forecasts through post-hoc residual adjustment.
analysis.main_results: The time-series foundation model TimesFM maintained comparatively stable probabilistic forecast performance at longer horizons, while most other models showed declining performance.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Together, these findings highlight the potential of pretrained representations for dengue forecasting, with benefits dependent on forecasting architecture, horizon and modelling configuration.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The largest improvements were observed for N-BEATS, including a reduction in mean WIS of 1.13 at the six-month horizon (95% CI [0.84, 1.48]; Diebold-Mariano p < 0.0001), with improvements also observed for XGBoost.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Covariate selection, spatial fitting and forecast aggregation strategies showed strong model-dependent effects, while monthly model retraining provided no consistent advantage in the settings evaluated.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of various forecasting models, including foundation models, in predicting monthly dengue cases across 5,570 Brazilian municipalities. The research highlighted the challenges of producing reliable forecasts across different time horizons and locations. The time-series foundation model TimesFM showed stable performance at longer horizons, while most other models declined. The study tested whether spatial representations of human and environmental context from a Population Dynamics Foundation Model (PDFM) could improve forecasts through post-hoc residual adjustment. PDFM adjustment improved mean probabilistic forecast performance, measured by the Weighted Interval Score (WIS), in 19 of 20 model-horizon combinations. The largest improvements were observed for N-BEATS, with a mean WIS reduction of 1.13 at the six-month horizon. The findings suggest that pretrained representations can enhance dengue forecasting, with benefits depending on the forecasting architecture, horizon, and modeling configuration. However, the study noted that covariate selection, spatial fitting, and forecast aggregation strategies had strong model-dependent effects, and monthly model retraining did not consistently improve outcomes. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the study's focus on model performance and the absence of direct biological or clinical data on dengue virus.

title: DISTRIBUIÇÃO ESPACIAL E TEMPORAL DA DENGUE EM CRIANÇAS E ADOLESCENTES EM SANTA CATARINA (2021–2025): SUBSÍDIOS PARA AÇÕES DE EDUCAÇÃO EM SAÚDE NO AMBIENTE ESCOLAR

analysis.research_question_and_background: O estudo foi conduzido para analisar a distribuição espacial e temporal dos casos prováveis de dengue em crianças e adolescentes, devido à maior epidemia registrada no país em 2024, com impacto significativo em Santa Catarina.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Trata-se de um estudo descritivo, quantitativo e retrospectivo, utilizando dados secundários e agregados por município de crianças e adolescentes residentes em Santa Catarina, na faixa etária de 5 a 19 anos, entre 2021 e 2025.
analysis.methods: Os dados foram obtidos junto ao CIEGES-SC e ao Censo 2022 do IBGE, sendo calculada a incidência dos casos por faixa etária e por macrorregião de saúde.
analysis.main_results: Foram registrados 109.918 (19,0%) casos na faixa etária de 5 a 19 anos, com o ano de 2024 concentrando o maior número de notificações, atingindo uma incidência estadual de 4.396,9 casos por 100/mil/hab. As faixas etárias de 5 a 9 anos (24,7%) e 15 a 17 anos (24,0%) foram as mais acometidas, enquanto as macrorregiões do Planalto Norte e Nordeste e do Vale do Itajaí concentraram, respectivamente, 35,3% e 34,3% dos casos.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Os resultados mostram uma distribuição heterogênea dos casos de dengue entre crianças e adolescentes, com concentração temporal em 2024 e em certas macrorregiões, indicando a necessidade de estratégias de educação em saúde direcionadas ao ambiente escolar.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: A distribuição espacial e temporal dos casos de dengue pode informar ações de vigilância epidemiológica e educação em saúde no ambiente escolar, contribuindo para a prevenção e controle da doença em populações vulneráveis.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: A evidência é baseada em dados secundários e agregados, o que pode limitar a precisão e a generalização dos resultados, mas a incidência calculada e a distribuição por faixa etária e região são consistentes com a metodologia descritiva utilizada.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed the spatial and temporal distribution of dengue cases in children and adolescents in Santa Catarina, Brazil, from 2021 to 2025. It aimed to provide insights for health education strategies in schools. The research used secondary data from CIEGES-SC and IBGE's 2022 census, aggregating cases by municipality and age group. Results showed that 19.0% of dengue cases occurred in children and adolescents, with 2024 being the peak year and the highest incidence rate of 4,396.9 cases per 100,000 inhabitants. The age groups 5-9 years and 15-17 years were most affected, and the Planalto Norte, Nordeste, and Vale do Itajaí macroregions had the highest case concentrations. The authors concluded that the heterogeneity in dengue distribution among children and adolescents highlights the need for targeted health education in schools. The study's findings are based on aggregated data, which may limit their precision and generalizability, but they provide valuable insights for public health interventions.

title: Các yếu tố khí hậu và ngưỡng đơn giản cho cảnh báo sớm sốt xuất huyết Dengue tại Việt Nam: góc nhìn One Health (“Climatic determinants” and simple thresholds for dengue early warning in Vietnam)

analysis.research_question_and_background: Nghiên cứu nhằm giải quyết vấn đề về sự thay đổi tính mùa của sốt xuất huyết Dengue do biến đổi khí hậu, đô thị hóa và biến đổi thủy văn, đồng thời chỉ ra rằng các ngưỡng dự báo dựa trên trung bình 5 năm không còn hiệu quả trong việc phát hiện dịch bệnh.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Nghiên cứu là một tổng quan ngắn (mini-review) dựa trên các tài liệu đã công bố, tập trung vào mối liên hệ giữa các yếu tố khí hậu và sốt xuất huyết Dengue tại Việt Nam và Đông Nam Á, bao gồm cả các thí nghiệm trên muỗi Aedes.
analysis.methods: Nghiên cứu đã trích xuất các ngưỡng khí hậu, chiều hướng nguy cơ, cơ chế tác động và thời gian báo trước từ 10 tín hiệu khí hậu, đồng thời đánh giá ba phương pháp dự báo (siêu tổ hợp xác suất, kênh dịch tễ, học máy) thông qua lăng kính One Health.
analysis.main_results: Nghiên cứu xác định 10 ngưỡng khí hậu với thời gian báo trước lên đến 6 tháng, có sự khác biệt theo vùng. Một số tín hiệu như hạn hán, biên độ nhiệt lớn và nắng nóng có thể làm tăng hoặc giảm nguy cơ dịch, tùy thuộc vào điều kiện cụ thể.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Tác giả cho rằng các tín hiệu khí hậu là lời kêu gọi sẵn sàng, không phải là lời dự báo chính xác, và đề xuất một hệ thống cảnh báo sớm kết hợp ba tầng để cải thiện khả năng ứng phó với dịch bệnh.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Kết quả có thể hỗ trợ thiết kế hệ thống cảnh báo sớm hiệu quả hơn, điều chỉnh nguồn lực dựa trên vùng và điều kiện khí hậu, từ đó nâng cao khả năng kiểm soát dịch sốt xuất huyết Dengue trong bối cảnh biến đổi khí hậu.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Nghiên cứu có hạn chế trong việc cần hiệu chỉnh ngưỡng bằng dữ liệu giám sát địa phương trước khi áp dụng, đồng thời các phương pháp dự báo có thể không hiệu quả trong các biến cố lớn như dịch COVID-19. Dựa trên các bằng chứng đã công bố, đánh giá là ở mức trung bình.

analysis.summary_en: Nghiên cứu này tập trung vào việc phân tích các yếu tố khí hậu ảnh hưởng đến sự bùng phát sốt xuất huyết Dengue tại Việt Nam trong bối cảnh biến đổi khí hậu và đô thị hóa. Các tác giả đã tổng hợp 10 ngưỡng khí hậu với thời gian báo trước lên đến 6 tháng, có sự khác biệt theo vùng. Họ nhấn mạnh rằng các ngưỡng dựa trên trung bình 5 năm không còn đáng tin cậy do gây báo động giả và bỏ sót dịch. Nghiên cứu đề xuất một hệ thống cảnh báo sớm kết hợp ba tầng, bao gồm mô hình xác suất, ngưỡng khí hậu và giám sát dịch tễ, nhằm cải thiện khả năng ứng phó với dịch bệnh. Tuy nhiên, các ngưỡng cần được hiệu chỉnh bằng dữ liệu địa phương trước khi triển khai. Mặc dù nghiên cứu cung cấp bằng chứng từ các tài liệu đã công bố, nhưng có hạn chế trong việc áp dụng trong các tình huống bất thường như dịch COVID-19. Kết quả có thể hỗ trợ thiết kế các hệ thống cảnh báo sớm hiệu quả hơn, điều chỉnh nguồn lực theo vùng và điều kiện khí hậu, từ đó nâng cao khả năng kiểm soát dịch sốt xuất huyết Dengue.

title: Evolutionarily distinct dengue virus type 2 with a unique type-specific neutralization determinant

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate whether genotypic differences in dengue virus type 2 (DENV2) strains, such as QML-22, are associated with antigenic differences. This is important because understanding antigenic variation can inform vaccine development and surveillance strategies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study characterized the antigenic features of QML-22, a divergent DENV2 strain, using antisera from infections with other DENV serotypes and non-human primates. The research focused on DENV2 and its relationship to other DENV serotypes.
analysis.methods: Antisera from non-human primates infected with QML-22 or DENV2 reference strain S16803 were used to assess neutralization. The 3F9 antibody, which targets a specific epitope in the envelope protein, was tested for its neutralization capacity against QML-22 and other DENV2 strains. Evolutionary analyses were conducted to compare the epitope's sequence across strains.
analysis.main_results: QML-22 was not as well neutralized by antisera against endemic DENV2 strains but was better neutralized by antisera from DENV1, 3, and 4 infections. The 3F9 epitope in QML-22 showed unique amino acids compared to the likely common ancestor of all DENV2 strains.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that the antigenic differences in QML-22 are significant and may contribute to its distinct neutralization profile. This highlights the antigenic diversification of DENV2 and raises the possibility of new serotypes evolving.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide insights into the antigenic evolution of DENV2, which could inform the development of more effective vaccines and improve surveillance strategies for emerging strains.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on abstract-only evidence, which may limit the depth of analysis. However, the findings are supported by direct experimental results and evolutionary comparisons, providing a moderate level of confidence.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the antigenic features of QML-22, a divergent dengue virus type 2 (DENV2) strain, and finds that it is not as well neutralized by antisera against endemic DENV2 strains but is better neutralized by antisera from DENV1, 3, and 4 infections. The 3F9 epitope in QML-22 shows unique amino acids compared to the likely common ancestor of all DENV2 strains. These findings suggest antigenic diversification within DENV2 and raise the possibility of new serotypes evolving. The study provides insights into the evolution of DENV2, which could inform vaccine development and surveillance strategies. However, the evidence is based on abstract-only data, which may limit the depth of analysis, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

title: Tetravalent dengue mRNA vaccination orchestrates balanced four-serotype immunity with durable memory and protection in mice.

analysis.research_question_and_background: An effective dengue vaccine must establish durable immunity across four dengue virus (DENV) serotypes, evade antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE), and overcome immune imprinting from prior exposure.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Here, we developed TetprM-E mRNA-LNP, a tetravalent vaccine comprising LNP-formulated nucleoside-modified mRNAs encoding DENV1-4 precursor membrane-envelope (prM-E) antigens, and evaluated its immunogenicity, durability, protection and breath across serotype-specific immune backgrounds.
analysis.methods: Three immunization strategies elicited neutralizing titers greater than 1:1500 against each serotype.
analysis.main_results: Passive transfer of immune sera conferred 100% survival and reduced viremia after lethal DENV2 challenge in immunocompromised mice.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Vaccination induced DENV envelope (env)-specific CD8+T cells and CD4-dependent germinal-center responses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: DENV env-binding antibodies persisted for 34 weeks alongside DENV env-specific memory B cells.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Vaccine-elicited sera showed no measurable in vitro ADE.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop an effective tetravalent dengue vaccine that provides durable immunity across all four serotypes while avoiding antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) and immune imprinting. The researchers created TetprM-E mRNA-LNP, a vaccine encoding DENV1-4 prM-E antigens, and evaluated its immunogenicity and protective capacity in mice. The vaccine induced high neutralizing titers against all serotypes and conferred complete survival and reduced viremia in immunocompromised mice after DENV2 challenge. Additionally, the vaccine elicited DENV envelope-specific CD8+ T cells and CD4-dependent germinal-center responses, with antibodies persisting for 34 weeks. The vaccine-elicited sera showed no measurable in vitro ADE, suggesting its potential to overcome immune imprinting. These findings demonstrate the vaccine's ability to generate broad, durable, and protective immunity against dengue despite pre-existing serologic constraints. The study's results are significant for vaccine development, as they highlight the effectiveness of a tetravalent mRNA-LNP vaccine in inducing immunity against all four DENV serotypes.

title: MicroRNA-based point-of-care diagnostics for emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases: from biomarker discovery to clinical implementation.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on the use of microRNA-based point-of-care diagnostics for dengue virus and dengue disease, including severe dengue, dengue hemorrhagic fever, dengue shock syndrome, dengue fever, and dengue virus 1–4. The central question is how miRNA signatures can be translated into clinically deployable diagnostics for these conditions.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review evaluates the diagnostic and translational potential of miRNAs across dengue virus and related diseases. It provides a cross-disease translational perspective, linking miRNA signatures with analytical and clinical validation, point-of-care development, clinical implementation, economic considerations, and deployment in resource-limited settings. The review does not explicitly report on meta-analysis or pooled estimates.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review highlights that miRNA-based diagnostics have potential for clinical implementation in dengue disease, particularly when integrated into affordable sample-to-answer platforms. It emphasizes the need for reproducible multi-miRNA signatures and standardized pre-analytical workflows to improve clinical utility.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is a lack of standardized pre-analytical workflows and prospective multicentre validation for miRNA-based diagnostics in dengue. The review also notes that continued biomarker discovery alone is insufficient for clinical deployment, and real-world conditions must be considered to demonstrate improved clinical decisions.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should prioritize the development of reproducible multi-miRNA signatures, standardized pre-analytical workflows, and prospective multicentre validation for miRNA-based diagnostics in dengue. These efforts are critical for translating miRNA research into practical, affordable point-of-care solutions.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the potential of microRNA-based point-of-care diagnostics for dengue virus and dengue disease, including severe dengue, dengue hemorrhagic fever, dengue shock syndrome, dengue fever, and dengue virus 1–4. It evaluates the translational potential of miRNA signatures, emphasizing the need for integration into affordable platforms and validation under real-world conditions. The review highlights that while miRNA research is promising, there are gaps in standardization and multicentre validation. It suggests that future efforts should focus on developing reproducible multi-miRNA signatures and improving pre-analytical workflows to enhance clinical utility. The review also notes that continued biomarker discovery alone is not sufficient for clinical deployment.

title: Etiological spectrum of acute encephalitis syndrome in children in India: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review aimed to estimate the pooled proportion of acute encephalitis syndrome (AES) cases attributable to various common infectious etiologies among children aged 18 years or younger in India. The central question focused on identifying the leading causes of pediatric AES, with a particular emphasis on dengue virus as the target entity.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A comprehensive search of PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Scopus was conducted for studies published between January 2000 and December 2025. The Joanna Briggs Institute checklist was used for quality assessment, and a random-effects model was employed to obtain pooled estimates and their corresponding 95% confidence intervals (CI).
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Scrub typhus and Japanese encephalitis (JE) viruses were identified as the leading identifiable etiologies of pediatric AES in India. Dengue virus was found to account for 5% of the cases (95%CI: 3%-8%).
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlighted that broader diagnostic methods, such as molecular techniques, may improve the diagnostic yield and enable early targeted therapy for children with AES. However, the evidence for dengue virus as a cause of AES was less prominent compared to other pathogens.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests the need for improved diagnostic methods and targeted therapies for dengue virus in pediatric AES cases. It also emphasizes the importance of further research to better understand the role of dengue virus in AES and to address diagnostic gaps.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to estimate the pooled proportion of acute encephalitis syndrome (AES) cases attributable to various infectious etiologies among children in India, with a focus on dengue virus. The review included 69 studies published between 2000 and 2025, sourced from PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Scopus. The findings indicated that scrub typhus and Japanese encephalitis (JE) viruses were the leading causes of AES, while dengue virus accounted for 5% of cases (95%CI: 3%-8%). The review also noted that broader diagnostic methods, such as molecular techniques, could enhance the identification of dengue virus in AES cases. However, the evidence for dengue virus was less robust compared to other pathogens, highlighting the need for further research and improved diagnostic strategies to better address the role of dengue in pediatric AES.

title: Immature Platelet Fraction in Viral Infections: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on dengue virus and its associated disease, specifically examining the role of the immature platelet fraction (IPF%) and absolute immature platelet count (IPC) as biomarkers in thrombocytopenia during viral infections. The central question is how these parameters are used across different dengue-related conditions and their clinical relevance.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review was conducted following PRISMA 2020 guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261501412). It searched PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library from January 2000 to May 2025 for observational studies of adults with viral infections, specifically those reporting IPF, IPC, or reticulated platelets. Methodological robustness was assessed using the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review synthesized 22 studies narratively. It found that in dengue, serial increases in IPF consistently preceded platelet recovery, although proposed thresholds varied. In contrast, higher immature platelet parameters in COVID-19 were associated with severity and mortality but were inconsistent after adjustment. The clinical value of these parameters appears to be disease- and outcome-specific.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Analytical heterogeneity and the absence of transferable thresholds currently limit the clinical implementation of IPF and IPC as biomarkers. Evidence in chronic hepatitis, HIV, hantavirus, and Crimean–Congo hemorrhagic fever was mainly pathophysiological, and data in critically ill patients were almost confined to COVID-19.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Further research is needed to establish consistent thresholds for IPF and IPC across different viral infections, particularly for dengue. There is a need for more robust studies to validate the prognostic use of these parameters in dengue and other related conditions.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review explores the use of immature platelet fraction (IPF%) and absolute immature platelet count (IPC) as biomarkers in thrombocytopenia associated with dengue virus infections. The review, following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, analyzed 22 observational studies from 2000 to 2025, focusing on adults with dengue-related conditions. It found that in dengue, serial IPF increases consistently preceded platelet recovery, though thresholds varied. In contrast, higher immature platelet parameters in COVID-19 were linked to severity and mortality but were inconsistent after adjustment. The clinical utility of these parameters appears to be disease-specific, with limited transferability across conditions. The review highlights the need for further research to standardize thresholds and validate their prognostic value in dengue and related viral infections.

title: Analysis of Cell Populations from Arbovirus-Infected Tissues by Flow Cytometry.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Arboviruses still represent a major challenge to public health in many parts of the world, yet each arboviral disorder displays distinct cellular tropism and activation patterns that remain not fully elucidated.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The supplied evidence does not report the study design, setting, dates, or population details.
analysis.methods: The authors describe flow cytometry as a tool that enables characterization of heterogeneous cell populations, assessment of activation and proliferation markers, quantification of inflammatory mediators, and detection of cell death pathways.
analysis.main_results: The supplied evidence does not report any direct observations or quantitative results.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors suggest that integrating flow cytometry parameters can enhance understanding of arbovirus pathogenesis, clarify cellular tropism, and elucidate immune responses to infection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The article outlines steps for applying flow cytometry to dengue-infected tissues, potentially improving surveillance and diagnostic approaches.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report any limitations or assess the strength of the evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This methodological article addresses the public‐health challenge posed by arboviruses, emphasizing that each virus exhibits distinct cellular tropism and activation patterns that are not fully understood. The authors propose flow cytometry as a versatile technique capable of profiling heterogeneous cell populations, measuring activation and proliferation markers, quantifying inflammatory mediators, and detecting cell‐death pathways in tissues infected with dengue, chikungunya, yellow fever, and Zika viruses. While the abstract does not provide specific experimental data, it outlines the main procedural steps for applying flow cytometry to dengue‐infected tissues, suggesting that such an approach could enhance understanding of dengue pathogenesis, clarify cellular tropism, and inform immune‐response studies. No study design, population details, results, or limitations are reported, limiting the ability to assess evidence strength. The work highlights a promising analytical strategy that may improve surveillance and diagnostic capabilities for dengue virus infection.

analysis.methods: This chapter examines whether residents living closer to a dengue-treating hospital are more likely to be detected as cases, using cross-sectional survey data from two Dhaka sites: Dhaka Community Medical College Hospital (Boro Moghbazar) and Mugdha Medical College Hospital.
analysis.main_results: Healthcare-worker responses revealed high knowledge but lower preventive practice, suggesting an institutional engagement gap.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: A divergent pattern in one distant zone coincided with localized drainage construction, suggesting environmental disturbances can temporarily override the proximity effect.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Having an affected neighbor was the strongest correlate of detection, indicating fine-scale spatial clustering.

analysis.summary_en: Detection declined significantly with distance, and the effect persisted after adjustment for awareness, age, and prior infection, with each additional 100 meters of distance lowering the odds of detection by roughly 5%. Dengue fever is a growing public health threat in urban Bangladesh, yet the role of hospital proximity as a spatial determinant of case detection remains largely untested. This chapter examines whether residents living closer to a dengue-treating hospital are more likely to be detected as cases, using cross-sectional survey data from two Dhaka sites: Dhaka Community Medical College Hospital (Boro Moghbazar) and Mugdha Medical College Hospital. Healthcare-worker responses revealed high knowledge but lower preventive practice, suggesting an institutional engagement gap. A divergent pattern in one distant zone coincided with localized drainage construction, suggesting environmental disturbances can temporarily override the proximity effect. Having an affected neighbor was the strongest correlate of detection, indicating fine-scale spatial clustering. This deterministic extraction is based on abstract only. The source does not explicitly report enough limitations for an independent appraisal, so confidence is low.

title: Pemberdayaan Masyarakat dengan Gerakan Pemberantasan Sarang Nyamuk (PSN) dan Survey Vektor DBD

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to improve students’ knowledge and awareness of dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF) prevention through the Mosquito Nest Eradication Movement (PSN), vector surveys, epidemiological investigations, and early detection of DHF.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The activity was conducted on August 29–30, 2026, at SMA Negeri 4 Manado, involving 60 students in collaboration with healthcare workers, Ranomut Community Health Center, the Manado City Health Office, and school representatives.
analysis.methods: The implementation methods included preparation, health education, vector surveys, follow-up actions, and evaluation.
analysis.main_results: The results showed that PSN education and vector surveys were conducted according to the planned topics.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The survey found no mosquito larvae in potential breeding sites within the school environment, which was attributed to the dry season.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This activity is expected to encourage students and school personnel to actively maintain environmental cleanliness and implement PSN measures sustainably.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The activity is expected to be sustainable, but the dry season may have influenced the absence of mosquito larvae.

analysis.summary_en: The study aimed to improve students’ knowledge of dengue prevention through PSN and vector surveys. Conducted at SMA Negeri 4 Manado, the activity involved 60 students and healthcare workers. Results showed successful implementation of planned topics, and no mosquito larvae were found due to the dry season. The activity is expected to encourage sustainable environmental cleanliness and PSN measures.

title: Pengaruh ekstrak rimpang temulawak (Curcuma xanthorrhiza Roxb) terhadap mortalitas larva Aedes albopictus

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever (DHF) is caused by the dengue virus (DENV), transmitted through of Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus. Larval control is essential to break transmission.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study used a quantitative true experimental design with a post-test only control group. Samples were selected through purposive sampling. The preparation of Curcuma xanthorrhiza rhizome extract was conducted at the Biomedical Laboratory I, Faculty of Medicine, Universitas Palangka Raya, while larvicidal testing was performed at the Public Health Laboratory Center, Tanah Bumbu, South Kalimantan, Indonesia, from July to October 2025.
analysis.methods: Temulawak rhizome extract was obtained through maceration using 96% ethanol. Larvae were tested at five concentrations (0.6%, 0.8%, 1.0%, 1.2%, and 1.5%) with observations at 3, 6, 12, and 24 hours. Data were analyzed using the Kruskal–Wallis test, Mann–Whitney post-hoc test, and probit analysis to determine LC50, LC90, LT50, and LT90.
analysis.main_results: Larval mortality increased with higher concentrations and longer exposure. The Kruskal–Wallis test showed significant differences among treatments (p < 0.05). LC50 was 0.614% and LC90 was 1.459%, while LT50 was 5.613 hours and LT90 was 15.102 hours.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The rhizome extract demonstrated effective larvicidal activity against third-instar Aedes albopictus larvae, with efficacy increasing according to extract concentration and exposure time. These findings provide scientific evidence supporting the potential use of C. xanthorrhiza as an environmentally friendly plant-based larvicide.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings contribute to the development of sustainable alternative strategies for dengue vector control.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations. The study design is a quantitative true experimental design with a post-test only control group, and the results are based on statistical analysis of larval mortality.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the larvicidal effectiveness of Curcuma xanthorrhiza Roxb extract against third-instar Aedes albopictus larvae. The research is motivated by the need for environmentally friendly alternatives to control dengue transmission, as Aedes albopictus is a key vector for dengue disease. The study employed a quantitative true experimental design with a post-test only control group, using purposive sampling. Temulawak rhizome extract was prepared via maceration with 96% ethanol and tested at five concentrations over specific exposure times. The results showed that larval mortality increased with higher concentrations and longer exposure, with significant differences among treatments (p < 0.05). The LC50 and LC90 values were 0.614% and 1.459%, respectively, while LT50 and LT90 were 5.613 hours and 15.102 hours. The findings suggest that the extract could be a viable, eco-friendly larvicide for dengue vector control.
